nodes.summary: Write $N(a + bi) = a^2 + b^2$ for the norm on $\mathbb{Z}[i]$. Let $p$ be a prime with $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$, let $e$ be a natural number, and suppose $\pi \in \mathbb{Z}[i]$ is a prime element with $N(\pi) = p$. Then exactly $4(e + 1)$ Gaussian integers $\alpha$ satisfy $|N(\alpha)| = p^e$.
nodes.title: Number of Gaussian integers of norm a power of a split prime

nodes.summary: A Gaussian integer $x \in \mathbb{Z}[i]$ is a unit if and only if $x$ is one of $1$, $-1$, $i$ and $-i$.
nodes.title: Units of the Gaussian integers

nodes.summary: Every prime element $z$ of the Gaussian integers $\mathbb{Z}[i]$ is associated to one of the following: a rational prime $p$ with $p \equiv 3 \pmod 4$; one of $a + bi$ and $a - bi$, where $a$ and $b$ are natural numbers with $a^2 + b^2 = p$ for some rational prime $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$; or $1 + i$.
nodes.title: Classification of the Gaussian primes

nodes.summary: Let $\pi = a + bi \in \mathbb{Z}[i]$ and let $N(\pi) = a^2 + b^2$ be its norm. If the absolute value of $N(\pi)$ is a prime number, then $\pi$ is a prime element of $\mathbb{Z}[i]$.
nodes.title: Gaussian integers of prime norm are prime

nodes.summary: The Gaussian integer $1 + i$ is a prime element of $\mathbb{Z}[i]$; its norm is $2$.
nodes.title: 1 + i is a Gaussian prime

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime, write $N(a + bi) = a^2 + b^2$ for the norm on $\mathbb{Z}[i]$, and let $\pi \in \mathbb{Z}[i]$ satisfy $N(\pi) = p$. Then $p = \pi \bar{\pi}$ in $\mathbb{Z}[i]$, where $\bar{\pi}$ is the complex conjugate of $\pi$, and $\bar{\pi}$ is a prime element of $\mathbb{Z}[i]$.
nodes.title: Factoring a prime as a Gaussian integer times its conjugate

nodes.summary: Write $N(a + bi) = a^2 + b^2$ for the norm on $\mathbb{Z}[i]$. Let $p$ be a prime with $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$ and let $\pi \in \mathbb{Z}[i]$ satisfy $N(\pi) = p$. Then the complex conjugate $\bar{\pi}$ is not associated to $\pi$: there is no unit $u$ of $\mathbb{Z}[i]$ with $\bar{\pi} u = \pi$.
nodes.title: Gaussian integers of split prime norm are not associate to their conjugates

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime with $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$. Then there are natural numbers $a$ and $b$ with $a^2 + b^2 = p$ such that both $a + bi$ and $a - bi$ are prime elements of the Gaussian integers $\mathbb{Z}[i]$.
nodes.title: Explicit Gaussian prime factors of a prime congruent to 1 mod 4

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime with $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$. Then there is a prime element $\pi = a + bi$ of $\mathbb{Z}[i]$ whose norm $N(\pi) = a^2 + b^2$ equals $p$.
nodes.title: Primes congruent to 1 mod 4 split in the Gaussian integers

nodes.summary: In $\mathbb{Z}[i]$ we have $2 = -i \cdot (1 + i)^2$, where $-i$ is a unit with inverse $i$.
nodes.title: Factorization of 2 in the Gaussian integers

nodes.summary: Let $u_0 = 1$, $u_1 = -1$, $u_2 = i$ and $u_3 = -i$. Every unit $u$ of $\mathbb{Z}[i]$ equals $u_j$ for some $j \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}$.
nodes.title: The enumeration of the Gaussian units is complete

nodes.summary: Let $u_0 = 1$, $u_1 = -1$, $u_2 = i$ and $u_3 = -i$ in $\mathbb{Z}[i]$. For $j, k \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}$, if $u_j = u_k$ then $j = k$.
nodes.title: The four Gaussian units are distinct

nodes.summary: The map $v$ on $\{0, 1, 2, 3\}$ with $v_0 = 1$, $v_1 = -1$, $v_2 = -i$ and $v_3 = i$ in $\mathbb{Z}[i]$, listing the inverses of the units $1$, $-1$, $i$ and $-i$ in that order.
nodes.title: Inverses of the Gaussian units
Each Gaussian unit times its listed inverse is one

nodes.summary: The map $u$ on $\{0, 1, 2, 3\}$ with $u_0 = 1$, $u_1 = -1$, $u_2 = i$ and $u_3 = -i$ in $\mathbb{Z}[i]$, listing the four units of $\mathbb{Z}[i]$.
nodes.title: Enumeration of the Gaussian units

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
